title: KL Rahul-backed Boldfit raises over Rs 400 Cr in Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund
summary:
Boldfit, a homegrown sports brand, has raised over Rs 400 crore (nearly $42 million) in its Series B funding round led by Bharat Value Fund, managed by The Wealth Company Alternates, part of the Pantomath Group. Existing investor Bessemer Venture Partners also participated in the round.
The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised Rs 110 crore, or around $13 million, in a funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners in November 2024. It also raised $8.37 million from existing investors, including KL Rahul.
The fresh funds will be used to drive growth, with investments planned in nationwide retail expansion, product innovation and manufacturing. The company will also selectively pursue inorganic opportunities to strengthen its presence and capabilities across categories, Boldfit said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani and Aasshna Guptaa, Boldfit is an e-commerce platform that offers sports and fitness products across categories such as apparel, fitness equipment, nutrition supplements and accessories. Its portfolio covers sports such as basketball, cycling, football, volleyball, badminton and cricket, with over 400 products.
The company said it serves over 2 crore customers annually. It is also strengthening its integrated product development and manufacturing capabilities, with a focus on innovation, quality and long-term competitive advantages.
Boldfit aims to build a sports brand for a billion Indians through product innovation, manufacturing and nationwide distribution, the company said.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. Its operating revenue jumped 2.17X to Rs 304 crore in FY25 from Rs 140 crore in FY24. Profit also surged 2.08X to Rs 35 crore in FY25 from Rs 16.82 crore in the previous fiscal.
In the sports and fitness segment, Agilitas, a sportswear platform, raised Rs 225 crore from Nexus Venture Partners and Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, in June 2026. The funds will be used to strengthen its manufacturing, brand-building, retail and technology capabilities.
Meanwhile, PlayBlue raised $2.7 million in seed funding in July 2026 from Centre Court Capital, MIXI Global and WEH Ventures to launch its omnichannel sports retail business, which will include a pan-India e-commerce platform and flagship stores.

title: Nazara’s Nitish Mittersain steps down as MD; Mithun Sacheti becomes executive director, Arun Agrawal named CFO
summary:
Nazara Technologies founder Nitish Mittersain will step down as managing director and transition to the role of founder and non executive director, months after stepping down as CEO. The company has also redesignated Mithun Padam Sacheti as an executive director and appointed a new chief financial officer (CFO).
The company’s board approved the changes at a meeting held on October 12, according to a stock exchange disclosure.
Mittersain, who founded Nazara in 1999, will move out of his executive responsibilities as managing director, subject to shareholder approval. He will continue to provide strategic guidance to the company.
In August 2026, Mittersain stepped down as CEO following the company’s Q1 FY27 results, which were hit by losses from associates and impairment charges.
Meanwhile, Nazara has redesignated Sacheti from non executive director to whole time director and key managerial personnel, subject to shareholder approval. Sacheti, the founder of jewellery brand CaratLane, will oversee strategic initiatives and operational responsibilities assigned by the board.
The company has also appointed Arun Agrawal as CFO from October 16, replacing Rakesh Shah, who will step down on October 15 to pursue a professional opportunity outside the company. 
Before joining Nazara, Agrawal served as global CFO at Ness Digital Engineering and held a senior finance role at Mastek. He has also worked with Firstsource Solutions, General Electric, Wipro and Tata Motors.
In another leadership change, whole time director Rohit Sharma will step down from his position with effect from January 11, 2027, to pursue entrepreneurial opportunities.
The leadership changes come as Nazara continues to expand its gaming portfolio. Separately, the board approved an investment of $77 million (around Rs 743 crore) in its UK subsidiary to fund the second tranche of consideration for its acquisitions of Bluetile Games and Bestplay Systems.
The board also approved the allotment of 2.39 crore equity shares at Rs 306 apiece to five investors on a preferential basis, raising around Rs 731 crore. In addition, it approved the conversion of outstanding loans worth up to Rs 129.35 crore extended to Smaaash Entertainment and a £23 million (around Rs 294.4 crore) loan extended to its UK subsidiary into equity.

title: InCred Capital appoints Abhinav Khanna as Capital Markets CEO, Abhimanyu Kalra as MD of Equities
summary:
InCred Capital has appointed Abhinav Khanna as CEO of Capital Markets and Abhimanyu Kalra as managing director and co-head of equities as it looks to expand its institutional equities business in India.
The appointments are part of the company’s efforts to grow its market share in India’s institutional equities segment multi-fold over the next five years, supported by investments in technology, execution infrastructure and international expansion, InCred Capital said in a press release.
Khanna brings over 25 years of experience across India, the UK and the Middle East. He most recently served as managing director and chief business officer at ValueQuest Investment Advisors. Before that, he spent over a decade at Citigroup Global Markets, where he was managing director and head of equities for India.
Kalra has over 23 years of experience in equity markets, including 18 years at Nomura, where he developed relationships with global and domestic asset managers.
The company has also launched its US business under Arunava Das, who joins as CEO of InCred Capital USA. Das previously served as CEO of JM Financial’s North America business and has held senior roles at JPMorgan Chase and Edelweiss Capital.
Alongside the leadership appointments, InCred Capital is investing in technology and execution infrastructure across order management, research distribution, institutional sales and trading, block execution and algorithmic trading.
The platform serves institutional clients, including mutual funds, insurance companies, pension funds, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), global long only investors and hedge funds.
“We are making a big bet on Capital Markets. India’s markets are getting larger, deeper and more important to global investors, while domestic institutional capital continues to grow rapidly,” said Bhupinder Singh, founder and group CEO of InCred.
Singh added that the company aims to build one of India’s leading institutional equities franchises.
InCred Capital is the institutional, wealth management and asset management arm of the InCred Group. It offers services across investment banking, institutional equities, wealth management and asset management.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 5- Oct 10]
summary:
This week, 28 Indian startups raised $113.35 million across 3 growth-stage deals, 22 early-stage deals, and 3 undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 8 key appointments, 3 fund launches and 2 mergers & acquisitions. 

In contrast, 24 startups had collectively secured about $411.46 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $55.3 million across three deals this week, led by lifestyle-tech brand DailyObjects, which secured Rs 332 crore (nearly $35 million) in a Series C round led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital.
Smart kitchen appliance startup Beyond Appliances raised Rs 110 crore ($11.4 million) in a Series B round led by Fireside Ventures, while MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth secured Rs 85 crore in equity and debt funding from FMO and LeapFrog Investments.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $58.05 million across 22 deals this week, led by photonic quantum technology startup Quanfluence, which secured $10 million from Chiratae Ventures and Rainmatter, followed by edtech startup byteXL with $9 million from Elevar Equity.
Medtech startup Sunfox Technologies raised $7 million in a Series A round co-led by Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, Alchemy Capital and 3one4 Capital, while quantum computing startup QpiAI secured Rs 50 crore in debt funding from InnoVen Capital.
Other funded startups included Omnichannel menswear brand Kisah, Wealth management startup Zomint, AI startup Desible.ai, healthtech SuperMush, Cold-pressed oil brand Gramiyaa, among others. 
Travel tech platform TravClan, financial information platform MoneyTruVa, and Biofortified staples brand Better Nutrition also raised funding this week but did not disclose the amounts.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru again led the funding charts with 10 startup deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR and Mumbai with 6 deals and 3 deals respectively. Hyderabad, Dehradun, Chandigarh and others also recorded deals.

E-commerce startups led the sectors with 8 deals, followed by AI and healthtech startups which grabbed 5 deals and 4 deals respectively. Meanwhile fintech, foodtech, SaaS, edtech, deeptech and others also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led the week with 13 deals, followed by pre-seed and Series A startups which grabbed 5 deals each. Series C, Series B, debt and pre-Series A recorded  a deal each.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding dropped over 72% to $113.35 million from $411.46 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $231.6 million across 22 deals.
[Key Hirings]
Eight key appointments were announced this week. Sorry Sugar named Palash Arneja as Founder and CEO, while Google Cloud appointed Amit Kumar as interim India head. Snabbit appointed Ramesh Srinivasan as Head of Growth and Revenue, ALTEN India named Prabhakar Atla as CEO, and Eggoz onboarded actor Boman Irani as its brand ambassador.
Meanwhile, Genefied promoted Krishna Khandelwal to Chief Sales Officer, Sarvam AI appointed former Google Cloud India MD Sashikumar Sreedharan as President and Chief Business Officer, and OTPless named Geetanshu Singla as CTO.
[Mergers and Acquisitions]
FMCG major Marico acquired an additional 24.09% stake in Plix parent Satiya Nutraceuticals for Rs 1,012.03 crore, while paediatric healthcare company Hoola Health acquired early-childhood development platform UpTodd.
[Fund Launches]
Entrepreneur Navya Naveli Nanda launched Naveli Ventures, the venture arm of the Nanda Family Office, to invest in deeptech, AI, clean energy, space and healthcare startups. Meanwhile, NABVENTURES secured Rs 450 crore in the first close of its second fund, while Recur Club announced a Rs 500 crore fund to provide growth capital to 150-170 D2C brands in FY27.
[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ PhonePe partners with DPCGC to strengthen regulatory compliance in OTT ecosystem
PhonePe has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Digital Publisher Content Grievances Council (DPCGC), a self-regulatory body under IAMAI, to strengthen regulatory compliance in the OTT ecosystem. The partnership aims to simplify self-regulatory organisation (SRO) certification for OTT platforms and online content publishers that use PhonePe’s payment gateway. It will also focus on merchant education and awareness of regulatory requirements under the IT Rules, 2021, which mandate SRO membership for grievance redressal.
▪️ Flipkart expands warehouse capacity by 14 Mn cubic feet ahead of festive season
Flipkart has expanded its supply chain ahead of the festive season, adding 14 million cubic feet of warehousing capacity and extending its delivery network to over 750 new PIN codes. The expansion increased storage capacity by 50%, while automation and technology upgrades boosted peak processing volumes by more than 30% ahead of its Big Billion Days sale.
▪️Pluckk takes its clean-label vision global with UK expansion
Digital-first FMCG brand Pluckk has entered the UK market, with its products available in 17 stores and a 15% share of the protein bar category at these outlets within the first month. The company aims to expand to 100 stores within three months and 500 within a year. It also plans to increase its UK portfolio to over 50 SKUs across clean-label categories, including juices, functional drinks, snacks and salads.
▪️ Pine Labs launches unified payments and customer engagement platform in Singapore
Pine Labs has launched a unified merchant platform in Singapore that combines payment acceptance, acquiring, installment payments and customer engagement services. The platform supports card and alternative payment methods, bank-backed installment plans and rewards through its Fave app. It aims to simplify merchant operations, improve checkout conversions and boost customer retention.
[News flash this week]
▪️ Startup Policy Forum’s DeepVerse platform brings together 30 investors and founders to shape deeptech policy
Startup Policy Forum (SPF) has launched DeepVerse, a deeptech policy platform with 30 partners, including Accel, Bessemer Venture Partners and Lightspeed. The initiative aims to address policy challenges across 10 sectors, including semiconductors, spacetech, defence technology, biotech, cleantech and robotics.
▪️ Flipkart’s Big Billion Days returns for 13th edition on October 9 with record seller participation
Flipkart has announced the 13th edition of its flagship festive sale, The Big Billion Days, starting October 9, with early access for select members on October 8. The sale will feature record seller participation, AI-powered shopping experiences and an expanded supply chain network of over 8,200 fulfilment and delivery facilities across India, including Ekart and Flipkart Minutes.
▪️Bengaluru to host Climate Data Week 2026 with over 30 events
The Climate Collective Foundation will host the first edition of Bangalore Climate Data Week from October 12 to 16, with over 30 events across Bengaluru. Supported by Google and Karnataka’s innovation bodies, the initiative is expected to attract over 2,000 participants, including climate tech founders, investors, researchers and policymakers, to explore the use of data and AI in addressing climate challenges.
▪️ Blinkit leads quick commerce in product availability, Flipkart Minutes ranks second: Bernstein
Eternal’s quick commerce arm Blinkit led India’s major quick-commerce platforms in product availability with an average in-stock rate of 94.4%, followed by Flipkart Minutes at 88.7%, Swiggy Instamart at 83.8% and Zepto at 82.5%, according to a report by brokerage firm Bernstein.
▪️ Groww adds over 1 lakh active clients in September, Sahi clocks 11% growth
Groww maintained its lead in India’s stock broking market in September 2026, adding over 1 lakh active clients, while Sahi recorded the fastest growth among the top 20 brokers at 11% month-on-month. According to NSE data, the industry’s active client base grew 0.35% to 4.61 crore from 4.60 crore in August, with nearly 1.6 lakh net additions.
▪️BofA cuts PB Fintech price target by 19%; anticipates strong Q2 for Paytm
BofA expects PB Fintech and Paytm to report strong Q2 FY27 growth but flagged regulatory risks for PB Fintech following IRDAI’s proposed changes to insurance commissions. The brokerage cut PB Fintech’s price target by 19% to Rs 1,145, citing a potential 39-41% decline in EPS in FY28 and FY29, while maintaining a Neutral rating. It retained its Buy rating on Paytm with a target price of Rs 1,775.

title: Exclusive: Nat Habit to kick off $15 Mn funding round led by Trident Growth Partners
summary:
Natural personal care D2C firm Nat Habit is raising Rs 142.6 crore ($15 million) in a fresh round led by Trident Growth Partners, with participation from Bertelsmann, Firstport, Linklight Ventures and others.
The board at Nat Habit is issuing 22.5 lakh Series C preference shares at an issue price of Rs 633.5 each to raise Rs 142.6 crore, according to its regulatory filing accessed from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Trident Growth Partners will be leading the round with Rs 91 crore, while Bertelsmann and Linklight Ventures will invest Rs 37 crore and Rs 6.8 crore, respectively. Mirabilis, Firstport and Dharmayug Investments will contribute the remaining amount.
According to the filings, the fresh proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, expansion, brand building and other requirements. Notably, Rs 2.6 crore from the total proceeds will also be used for the reduction of the ESOP pool.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the post-money valuation of the firm stood at around Rs 800 crore.
Moneycontrol reported on Nat Habit’s fresh funding in July.
Following the fresh issue, Trident Growth Partners will hold an 11.44% stake in the company, while existing investor Bertelsmann will hold 17.54% of the cap table. As per the filing, before the fresh issue, Swagatika Das and Gaurav Agarwal held 16% each in the firm.
Nat Habit has rebranded itself as Breathe Life, marking a shift in its positioning from an Ayurvedic brand to a broader lifestyle proposition. The company sells Ayurvedic personal care products, including shampoos, face washes, and moisturisers.
The company is yet to file its annual statements for FY26. During FY25, its revenue from operations grew 47.2% year-on-year to Rs 106 crore, while its losses increased to Rs 29 crore in the same period.

title: OTPless appoints former BharatPe, Genwise exec Geetanshu Singla as CTO
summary:
Bengaluru-based identity and access management startup OTPless has appointed former BharatPe technology head and Genwise co-founder Geetanshu Singla as its Chief Technology Officer (CTO).
In his new role, Singla will lead engineering, product development, platform architecture, reliability and security across OTPless’s authentication and fraud prevention stack, which includes Silent Network Authentication, WhatsApp authentication, device intelligence and passkeys.
Singla was previously Vice President of Technology at BharatPe, where he worked closely with OTPless co-founders Satyam Nathani and Tanmay Sagar during the fintech’s early growth. He later co-founded Genwise, which shut down its operations in December last year.
The appointment follows a series of leadership changes at OTPless. On September 18, the company elevated Nathani as CEO and Sagar as COO. On October 1, it appointed early team member Manas Poddar as Chief Business Officer (CBO).
OTPless claims to authenticate over 300 million users across consumer platforms such as Meesho, Zepto, Navi, PhysicsWallah, ShareChat, Shiprocket and ixigo. The company has grown its topline 2.5X over the past year to Rs 36 crore in annualised revenue and has been break-even for the past two quarters..
“The businesses we serve are some of India’s largest consumer platforms, and for them, login is the front door to their entire business. A failed or slow authentication is a lost customer, so they need technology they can rely on at any scale, on any day. Geetanshu has built and run technology at unicorn scale, and his joining strengthens the technical trust our customers place in us,” said Sagar.
Singla said he had worked closely with Nathani and Sagar during his time at BharatPe and described joining OTPless as coming back home. He added that the company’s expansion from OTP authentication to a broader identity and trust layer presents a significant opportunity.
Founded in 2023, OTPless provides authentication and identity infrastructure to consumer internet companies. Its platform enables user verification through Silent Network Authentication, WhatsApp authentication, device intelligence and passkeys, reducing reliance on SMS-based one-time passwords.
The company has raised over $6 million from investors including Venture Highway, White Venture, FJ Labs, SIDBI and Piper Serica.

NABVENTURES, the venture capital arm of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has secured commitments of Rs 450 crore in the first close of its second fund.

NABVENTURES Fund II will invest in early and growth-stage companies working across agriculture, food, agribusiness and rural markets. 
Its focus areas include agritech, rural fintech, climate-smart solutions, supply chain and logistics, and other businesses addressing challenges across the agricultural value chain.
The fund plans to back companies using technology and scalable business models to improve agricultural productivity, strengthen supply chains and support rural enterprises. It will also focus on solutions related to sustainability, climate resilience, financial inclusion and livelihood creation.
Along with capital, NABVENTURES plans to leverage NABARD’s nationwide presence and sectoral expertise to help portfolio companies expand their operations and reach rural markets.
The new fund builds on NABVENTURES’ earlier funds, which have collectively backed 23 enterprises. Through Fund II, the firm aims to support businesses that combine commercial growth with solutions for India’s agriculture and rural economy.

title: Rajan Anandan, Saurabh Srivastava author new book on India’s startup ecosystem
summary:
India’s startup ecosystem is entering a potential golden age, driven by a growing pool of experienced founders, innovation across sectors, increasing global ambitions, deeper capital markets and government support, according to The Lift-Off Nation: Why We Are Entering the Golden Age of Indian Startups, a new book by Rajan Anandan and Saurabh Srivastava.
Published by Juggernaut Books, the book argues that India’s startups, with a combined valuation of more than $400 billion, have achieved in roughly a decade what the country’s IT services industry took 35 years to accomplish in building a $325 billion sector.
The book draws on more than 180 interviews with founders, CEOs, investors, policymakers and academics to examine the factors shaping India’s startup ecosystem and its potential to become a global innovation hub.
Anandan is managing director at Peak XV Partners and former head of Google India and Southeast Asia, while Srivastava is a co-founder of NASSCOM, TiE and the Indian Angel Network.
The authors identify five factors that they believe are creating opportunities for Indian entrepreneurship.
The first is the emergence of experienced founders. Early Indian startups such as Flipkart, InMobi and Zoho have served as training grounds for talent, helping employees develop the skills needed to build and scale businesses. The second is the expansion of innovation across sectors.
The third factor is the growing global ambition of Indian startups, followed by the availability of venture capital and access to public markets. The fifth is the government’s role in enabling entrepreneurship. Regulatory reforms and digital public infrastructure, including Aadhaar and the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), have helped businesses establish and scale operations.
The book notes that India has more than 400 space-tech startups, six years after the sector was opened to private participation in 2020.
India spends approximately 0.65% of its gross domestic product (GDP) on research and development (R&D), compared with 2.6% in China and 3.5% in the US, according to figures cited in the book. The authors argue that India needs to raise R&D expenditure to at least 3% of GDP to compete in technology-intensive industries and build globally competitive businesses driven by innovation.

title: Exclusive: Gramiyaa raises fresh capital in Series A round at Rs 110 Cr valuation
summary:
Bengaluru-based cold-pressed oil brand Gramiyaa has raised Rs 18.65 crore in a Series A funding round led by new investor Optiscape Network Holdings and participation from existing investors Homegrown Ventures, Campus Fund  and others.

In March 2025, the company had raised Rs 7.2 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Homegrown Ventures, with participation from Campus Fund and Mumbai Angels.
According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the company’s board has allotted 32,968 Series A CCPS at Rs 5,657 per share to raise the fresh capital.
Optiscape Network Holdings led the round with an investment of Rs 9 crore, followed by Homegrown Ventures with Rs 4.5 crore and Campus Fund with Rs 4 crore.
Sarya Global Holdings invested Rs 90 lakh, while Rasagna Pulapaka contributed Rs 25 lakh in the round.

The Mumbai-based company had previously raised Rs 300 crore ($36 million) in a Series D equity round in December 2022, led by FMO along with existing investors.
The latest proceeds will be used to grow its loan book to nearly Rs 3,000 crore before the company requires another equity infusion, NeoGrowth said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2011 by Dhruv Khaitan and Piyush Khaitan, NeoGrowth provides business loans tailored to the needs of small businesses. Its offerings include both collateral-free and collateral-based loans for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
The company uses technology and data analytics to assess borrowers based on digital payment data, point-of-sale (POS) transactions and cash flows rather than relying solely on traditional collateral. It also offers flexible repayment schedules, with daily, weekly, fortnightly and monthly collection options.
NeoGrowth claims to operate in more than 25 cities across India, serving over 80 business segments and more than 1 lakh businesses.
Digital lenders are increasingly using GST records, banking transactions, digital payment trails and other business data to assess creditworthiness and extend loans to kirana stores, manufacturers, traders, distributors and small service providers.
The segment has attracted investor interest as lenders target underserved MSMEs through supply chain financing and embedded credit solutions.
Recent funding activity reflects this trend. In February 2026, Prayaan Capital raised Rs 110 crore in a Series A round led by Peak XV Partners to build its technology-led MSME lending platform. In August 2026, GetVantage secured Rs 63 crore in Series A1 funding to scale its cash flow-based financing platform for businesses.
Meanwhile, Business Nextgen Finance raised Rs 215 crore in equity to expand its technology-enabled secured lending operations for underserved MSMEs. Other notable fundraises include FlexiLoans, which raised Rs 375 crore in a Series C round in June 2025, and Techfino, which secured Rs 65 crore in June 2025 to expand its technology-enabled lending business in smaller cities.

title: GST Council removes arrest powers, raises prosecution threshold to Rs 5 Cr
summary:
The GST Council has recommended a series of changes to simplify compliance for businesses and reduce the involvement of tax officials. The decisions were taken at the 57th GST Council meeting held on Thursday, October 8.
The Council has recommended removing the arrest provisions under GST and raising the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore. It has also proposed reducing the general penalty from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000.
The government will also make the GST refund process faster. The timeline for issuing an acknowledgement or deficiency memo will be reduced from 15 days to 10 days. For eligible refund claims related to zero-rated supplies and inverted duty structure, 90% of the claimed amount will be sanctioned provisionally through a risk-based system without officer intervention.
The Council has also suggested simplifying GST registration and compliance. Routine registration changes will be processed automatically, while the government plans to introduce common standards for GST notices and proceedings.
For goods moving between states, physical interception will be restricted to cases based on specific intelligence and authorised by a senior tax officer.
Small sellers using e-commerce platforms will also get an easier route to register in another state. They will be allowed to use an e-commerce operator’s warehouse as their principal place of business, subject to certain conditions.
On input tax credit (ITC), the Council has widened relief for genuine taxpayers. However, the proposal to allow businesses to claim ITC even when their suppliers have not deposited the tax has been referred to a committee for further examination.
The Council has not announced any GST rate changes this time. The process reforms are expected to be implemented from April 1, 2027.

title: DailyObjects raises Rs 332 Cr in Series C round led by Xponentia, Anicut, Axiom Asia
summary:
Design-led lifestyle-tech brand DailyObjects has raised Rs 332 crore (nearly $35 million) in a Series C funding round led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital.
The round, which comprised primary and secondary transactions, valued the company at around Rs 1,050 crore. The company plans to use the capital to expand its retail network, invest in product development and R&D, strengthen brand building and explore international markets.
As part of the round, early investor Roots Ventures partially exited DailyObjects with an 18X return on its investment. It will continue to remain a shareholder in the company alongside 360 One Asset and Trifecta Capital.
DailyObjects plans to open 150 exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) across India over the next five years. The company currently has nearly 350 retail touchpoints, including EBOs and Apple Premium Reseller outlets.
The company will also invest in new product ranges, design, materials, quality and R&D across its existing categories. DailyObjects started with phone cases and has expanded into technology accessories, carry and workspace products.
Founded in 2012 by Pankaj Garg and Saurav Adlakha, DailyObjects has built a portfolio spanning technology, carry, workspace and lifestyle products. The company said it remains focused on capital efficiency and profitable growth as it scales its retail and product operations.
DailyObjects has raised nearly $50 million in funding to date, with Seedfund and 360 One Ventures among its key investors. The company last raised $10 million in May 2024.
Before the latest round, DailyObjects had raised around Rs 100 crore in equity over the past decade to build and scale its business.
DailyObjects' operating revenue rose 31% to Rs 110 crore in FY25 from Rs 84 crore in FY24, according to the company's financials. However, its total expenses increased 29.7% to Rs 124.5 crore during the year from Rs 96 crore in FY24. As a result, the company's loss widened to Rs 16 crore in FY25 from Rs 10 crore in FY24.
The company had earlier projected FY26 revenue of Rs 230-244 crore and aimed to achieve EBITDA profitability. It plans to support this through its owned channels, exclusive stores, airport retail presence and distribution across more than 250 Apple Premium Reseller stores.
DailyObjects is also evaluating international markets and is currently in the R&D and exploration stage. It expects to potentially make a more concrete move into overseas markets from the next financial year.

title: Palash Arneja takes charge as Founder and CEO of Sorry Sugar
summary:
Zero-added-sugar beverage brand Sorry Sugar has appointed Palash Arneja as its Founder and CEO. 
Arneja had earlier incubated the brand with Wolfpack Labs and will now lead its product, distribution and business growth strategy.
The development follows the recent funding round of Sorry Sugar. Last month, it raised  $1 million in a seed funding round led by the Dhanuka family and Amishi London.
Arneja previously built BLA BLI BLU, which the company said scaled to Rs 1,000 crore in under a year. Before that, he was associated with Unikon.ai, Deloitte and HSBC.
Sorry Sugar currently operates in the flavoured coffee segment, offering products positioned as zero-added-sugar, prebiotic and fibre-rich. The brand uses monk fruit as a sweetener along with prebiotic fibre.
The company plans to expand its presence across online and offline channels and move beyond coffee into other everyday consumption categories. Arneja will oversee product development, market expansion and the broader business strategy as part of this expansion.
Sorry Sugar was initially incubated with Wolfpack Labs. Under Arneja’s leadership, the company plans to build a broader portfolio focused on reducing added sugar in everyday consumption while expanding its presence in India.

title: Pet food startup TailBlaze Longevity raises pre-seed funding
summary:
Pet food startup TailBlaze Longevity has raised $300K in a pre-seed funding round led by US-based VC firm Comma Capital. The startup was also featured on Bharat Ke Superfounders.
The fresh capital will be used to launch HeartPour, build a team in Ahmedabad, and expand its reach among pet parents across India. Before the launch, the startup plans to offer the first 500 dogs a free serving of HeartPour, TailBlaze Longevity said in a press release.
Founded in August last year by Manaal Maniyar and Palak Devpura, TailBlaze is a pet care startup focused on canine longevity and nutrition. The startup aims to extend dogs’ lives by 3–5 years through high-protein and lower-carbohydrate nutritional formulations.
According to the Ahmedabad-based startup, HeartPour is a wet dog food line developed over four years of R&D. The product combines high protein and superfoods with an Ayurvedic PanchTatva blend comprising curcumin, black pepper, parsley, amla and tulsi.
The startup has also developed FreshTail, a proprietary technology for manufacturing shelf-stable fresh meals. Its portfolio includes more than 200 products across organic dog food, natural treats such as coconut and hemp or fish and strawberry, grooming essentials, and accessories.
TailBlaze Longevity follows a WhatsApp-first commerce model and also sells through quick commerce and online platforms such as Blinkit and BBNow.
In the pet nutrition segment, Right4Paws is developing science-based, species-specific whole-food nutrition focused on pet health and longevity. The startup raised Rs 14 crore in Series A funding in December last year to expand manufacturing, R&D, specialised talent and functional products.
Benny’s Bowl, another nutrition-focused startup, raised $1.4 million in February this year to develop functional pet foods for areas such as gut health, allergies, renal health, skin and coat health, and weight management.
Meanwhile, Zoomies raised Rs 5 crore in pre-seed funding in March this year to expand its clean-label, human-grade pet food business. Broader pet care platforms such as Supertails, which raised $30 million in Series C funding, are also expanding into technology, personalised care and healthcare services.

title: Blinkit leads quick commerce in product availability, Flipkart Minutes ranks second: Bernstein
summary:
Eternal's quick commerce arm Blinkit has emerged as the leader in product availability among India's major quick-commerce platforms, with an average in-stock rate of 94.4%, ahead of Flipkart Minutes, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto, according to a report by brokerage firm Bernstein.
The report found that Flipkart Minutes ranked second with 88.7% product availability, followed by Swiggy Instamart at 83.8% and Zepto at 82.5%. 

Bernstein conducted the study across 150 stock-keeping units (SKUs), covering grocery, fresh and non-grocery categories. The analysis tracked product availability over 10 days, across seven time slots per day and at least three PIN codes each in Mumbai, Gurugram and Bengaluru.
The report also noted Blinkit's consistent stock availability across days and time slots. While Blinkit maintained availability of around 94-95% throughout the observation period, Instamart and Zepto witnessed sharper fluctuations, with availability falling below 80% at certain intervals.
Instamart recorded the sharpest decline in product availability as the day progressed, at 11%, followed by Zepto at 6%. Blinkit and Flipkart Minutes recorded the lowest decline at 5% each. Bernstein attributed Instamart's higher decline to challenges in demand forecasting and inventory replenishment.
According to Bernstein, product availability is emerging as a key competitive differentiator in India's quick-commerce market, where platforms have traditionally competed on delivery speed and pricing.
The report noted that maintaining high availability requires effective demand forecasting, dark-store management, reliable procurement, and logistics operations.
Bernstein believes Blinkit's operational advantage could improve customer retention and reduce churn, as customers increasingly prefer platforms that can fulfill their entire shopping baskets.
On the financial front, Blinkit reported revenue of Rs 15,664 crore in Q1 FY27, while Swiggy Instamart recorded Rs 1,232 crore during the quarter. Zepto, meanwhile, posted revenue of Rs 22,624 crore in FY26. Blinkit and Zepto follow inventory-led models, while Instamart primarily operates under a marketplace model, which results in different revenue recognition.

Delhi NCR based lab-grown diamond jewellery brand Zinara has raised Rs 3.61 crore ($380K) in a pre-seed round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV). 
Nine Jewellery, Bollywood actress Nikita Dutta and other angel investors also participated in the round.
The proceeds will be used to expand its team, increase marketing activities and strengthen its supply chain infrastructure. It plans to expand its product and brand presence across India.
Founded by Harshit Abrol and Sumanyu Vyas, Zinara focuses on everyday diamond jewellery made with lab-grown diamonds and 18K gold vermeil. The firm currently has more than 400 designs and has crossed Rs 1 crore in annual recurring revenue.

title: Groww adds over 1 lakh active clients in September, Sahi clocks 11% growth
summary:
Stock broking platform Groww maintained its lead in India's stock broking market in September 2026, adding over 1 lakh active clients during the month. Meanwhile, discount broking platform Sahi continued to record the fastest growth among the top 20 stock brokers, with an 11% month-on-month increase in its active client base.
According to data from the National Stock Exchange (NSE), the total active client base increased marginally by 0.35% to 4.61 crore in September from 4.60 crore in August, an addition of nearly 1.6 lakh clients.

Groww retained its dominant position with 1.34 crore active clients in September, an addition of 1,00,961 clients compared to August. Its market share stood at 29.16%, the highest among stock brokers in India.
Zerodha remained the second-largest stock broker with 67.91 lakh active clients, despite a marginal decline of 5,313 clients during the month. Its market share stood at 14.73%.
Angel One followed closely in third position with 67.55 lakh active clients, an addition of 36,956 clients in September. The company's market share stood at 14.65%, marginally behind Zerodha.
ICICI Securities retained fourth position with 21.60 lakh active clients, an increase of 4,410 clients, while Upstox remained fifth with 18.54 lakh clients after losing 10,343 clients during the month.
Among other major brokers, Kotak Securities had 13.92 lakh active clients, followed by HDFC Securities with 13.54 lakh. 
Dhan recorded the third-highest net addition among the top 10 NSE brokers during September, adding 13,624 active clients to reach 11.2 lakh active clients. Meanwhile SBI Securities saw its client base decline by 22,525 to 10.21 lakh in September.
Paytm Money recorded one of the steepest declines among the top 20 brokers, losing 27,950 active clients, a 3.53% month-on-month drop, to reach 7.63 lakh. In contrast, INDmoney added 5,070 clients to reach 7.19 lakh in September.
Sahi emerged as the fastest-growing broker among the top 20 for another consecutive month, with an 11.1% increase in its active client base. The platform added 28,077 clients to reach 2.81 lakh, while its market share stood at 0.61%.
Choice also recorded strong growth of 2.88%, with an addition of 6,781 active clients. Meanwhile, PhonePe's Share.Market added 1,457 demat accounts in September.
The September data highlights the continued dominance of large discount brokers, with Groww accounting for over 63% of the industry's net client additions. The top five brokers collectively controlled more than 67% of the active client base, while smaller platforms such as Sahi continued to post faster percentage growth despite their relatively limited market share.

title: Info Edge posts Rs 822 Cr Q2 FY27 billings
summary:
Info Edge, the parent company of Naukri and 99acres, saw its standalone billings rise 12.8% year-on-year to Rs 822.3 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 729 crore in the same quarter last year, according to the stock exchange data.
For the first six months of FY27, Info Edge’s billings grew 13.5% to Rs 1,559.3 crore, from Rs 1,373.2 crore in the same period last year.
Its recruitment business, which includes Naukri, remained the biggest part of the company’s business. Billings from this segment grew 12.6% to Rs 613.8 crore in Q2 FY27, from Rs 545 crore a year ago. Info Edge said the business would have grown around 14-15% if the impact of customer renewal timings is removed.
99acres also reported strong growth. Its billings increased 21.2% to Rs 148.3 crore from Rs 122.4 crore in Q2 FY26. The growth was also higher than the 16.5% growth reported in the previous quarter.
In the matchmaking business, Jeevansathi’s billings grew 18.4% to Rs 39.7 crore. Aisle, another matchmaking platform owned by Info Edge, saw its billings grow 40%. Together, the matchmaking business grew 23.1% during the quarter.
However, Shiksha remained under pressure, with billings falling 27.2% to Rs 20.5 crore. Info Edge said AI-powered search is reducing the number of users coming to the platform through search engines. The company is working on new products to reduce its dependence on search traffic.
Info Edge also said more customers are using its B2B AI products, AI-Rex and Talent Pulse, with both products seeing growth in new customers and revenue.
The share price of the firm is currently trading at Rs 1205.5 (as of 10:14 AM), with the total market capitalization of 78,400 crore.

title: Google Cloud names Amit Kumar interim India head after Sreedharan exit
summary:
Google Cloud has appointed Amit Kumar as the interim head of its India operations following the departure of Sashikumar Sreedharan, who is leaving the company to pursue an external opportunity.
The leadership transition was announced by Karan Bajwa, President, Asia Pacific at Google Cloud. Bajwa said the company’s momentum in India remains strong, driven by growth in business and artificial intelligence (AI).
Sreedharan had been serving as Managing Director of Google Cloud India since July 2025. Before taking charge of the India business, he served as Chief Operating Officer for Google Cloud’s Asia Pacific region for around two years. He had been with Google Cloud for about three years.
Kumar, who has been with Google Cloud for more than five years, will take over the India leadership role on an interim basis. He currently serves as Managing Director of the company’s Digital Natives business in India, where he works with digital native companies and startups.
Kumar joined Google Cloud in March 2021 as a Sales Director and has spent nearly a year leading its Digital Natives business. Before joining Google Cloud, he was Country Sales Manager for Enterprise and Education at Apple India. He also held a leadership role at IBM and spent more than 13 years at Microsoft across product, enterprise sales and partner focused roles. Earlier in his career, he worked with Tata Telecom.
Announcing the transition, Bajwa said Google Cloud would remain focused on building on its momentum in India, adding that the opportunity for its customers and partners in the country has never been bigger.
The leadership change comes as India emerges as a key market for cloud and AI adoption, with Google Cloud competing for enterprise and startup customers alongside Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure.
Sreedharan’s exit also comes amid developments in India’s AI ecosystem. According to a Times of India report, Sreedharan is set to join homegrown AI unicorn Sarvam AI as President and Chief Business Officer.
Kumar’s interim appointment puts an executive with experience across enterprise sales, digital native businesses and technology companies at the helm of Google Cloud’s India operations as the company looks to sustain growth in cloud and AI.

Electric two wheeler maker Ola Electric will open its Rs 1,000 crore rights issue on October 22. The issue will close on October 30, 2026.
The company will issue 37.03 crore partly paid up equity shares at Rs 27 per share. This includes a premium of Rs 17 per share. The issue will raise Rs 999.74 crore if fully subscribed.
Ola Electric has fixed October 13 as the record date for determining shareholders eligible for the rights issue. Eligible shareholders will receive two rights shares for every 25 shares held on the record date.
Investors will pay Rs 16.20 per share at the time of application, while the remaining Rs 10.80 per share will be payable through a first and final call. The call is expected to be completed by October 31, 2027.
Ola Electric promoter Bhavish Aggarwal has pledged a 4.32% stake in the company to fund his participation in the rights issue. The pledge was created to fund his subscription, with no shares being sold as part of the transaction.
Ola Electric had earlier approved the proposed rights issue of up to Rs 1,000 crore on September 28. The company had also raised Rs 780 crore through a QIP in June to strengthen its balance sheet and support its growth plans.

summary:

The brand will use a mix of company owned outlets, select dine in formats and franchise partnerships as part of its expansion strategy.

title: Energy management platform Ionage raises $1.3 Mn in pre Series A round
summary:
AI enabled energy management platform Ionage has raised $1.3 million in a pre Series A funding round co-led by strategic investors and a consortium of CXOs from energy and infrastructure companies.
The fresh funds will be used to expand coverage to 100% of active EV charging networks in India, improve charger discovery and payments for EV users, and help small and mid sized charge point operators (CPOs) set up and manage station operations, Ionage said in a press release.
Founded in 2021 by Vimal Kumar V and Varun Chandran, Ionage is building an EV charging operating system that connects charge point operators, charger manufacturers, real estate owners and EV users. The platform enables drivers to discover, access and pay for charging across different charging networks.
According to the Bengaluru based startup, it has onboarded more than 25,000 four wheeler charge points and supports over 63 fleets across the country. It has a network of more than 75 charging partners and uses charger mapping and roaming capabilities to connect charging infrastructure across networks.
Ionage said it is on track to process more than 20 million units of energy per month over the next 12 months, supported by monthly growth of over 25%.
The startup operates across more than 70% of India’s charging hardware and connects with major EV charging manufacturers at the point of installation. Its solutions cater to offices, malls, hospitality businesses and residential housing societies.
Ionage currently operates across 33 states and Union Territories and nearly 3,000 cities. It plans to develop and support CPO micro clusters in Tier 2 cities over the next 18 months.
India’s EV charging infrastructure needs to grow more than 40 times by 2030 to meet demand, according to research by CII and ORF. The country will require more than 1.32 million public chargers by 2030 to support the expected 30 million plus electric two wheelers and four wheelers on the road.
Ionage offers products including Nexus, Ionage App, Flo and CASA, along with a Discovery API and business SDK that are currently in closed beta. The startup has also started using AI and ML capabilities for load balancing and energy trading across its charging network.

title: Exclusive: Green SM parent infuses Rs 153 Cr in Indian subsidiary to scale EV ride-hailing
summary:
Vietnam-based electric mobility startup Green SM has infused Rs 152.65 crore into its Indian subsidiary through a rights issue, marking another significant capital infusion as the company looks to scale its operations in the country.
The latest infusion comes after Green SM pumped Rs 85 crore into its Indian subsidiary in June 2026, taking its total investment in the country to nearly Rs 238 crore.
According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the board of GREEN SM INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED approved the allotment of 15.27 crore equity shares at Rs 10 per share to its parent entity, GSM Green and Smart Mobility Joint Stock Company, raising Rs 152.65 crore.
The company said the fresh capital will be used to expand its existing operations and scale its business activities in India. The infusion is expected to support Green SM as it builds its EV fleet and expands its ride-hailing network.
Green SM entered India in June 2026 with the launch of Green SM Limo, a fully electric taxi service, initially targeting the Delhi-NCR market.
Green SM is the electric mobility arm of Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup and operates its ride-hailing business under the Green SM brand. Founded in Vietnam in April 2023, the company has expanded to markets including Laos, Indonesia, the Philippines, India and Kazakhstan.
In India, Green SM is looking to tap the space left by BluSmart, which shut down its ride-hailing operations in 2025. Similar to BluSmart, Green SM operates an all-electric fleet with a company managed model, rather than relying on the traditional aggregator model followed by other established players such as Ola, Uber and Rapido.

title: Tanglin Venture leads Rs 16.1 Cr seed round in debt resolution platform Credfix
summary:
AI-first debt resolution platform Credfix has raised Rs 16.1 crore in a seed funding round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, with participation from Stargazer.
Before this round, Credfix had raised Rs 4.5 crore from K2 Capital, Invstt Trust and a group of angel investors.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate product development, strengthen its AI capabilities and expand its borrower support network across India, Credfix said in a press release.
Founded in 2025 by Ranjan Agarwal, Neeraj Kulkarni and Ayush Kedia, Credfix is an AI-powered financial recovery platform that helps borrowers understand their debt, assess repayment options and navigate interactions with lenders. Its offerings include debt assessment, loan resolution, loan consolidation and AI-powered legal assistance.
The platform has three key AI-led solutions: Risi, an AI financial assistant; Neytra, an AI call shield; and an AI legal assistant. Risi helps borrowers understand their debt and explore resolution options, while Neytra assists with recovery-related calls. The legal assistant helps borrowers understand legal notices, prepare draft responses for their review and identify possible next steps.
Credfix said it aims to support borrowers across the debt resolution lifecycle, from early signs of financial distress to structured resolution and financial rehabilitation. The platform helps users assess their financial obligations, evaluate available options, communicate with lenders and understand legal notices.
The startup claims to currently serve more than 2 lakh borrowers representing over Rs 4,000 crore in aggregate outstanding debt. Around 40% of its users are from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
The debt resolution and collections segment has seen growing technology adoption in India. FREED, a borrower-focused debt relief platform, raised Rs 60 crore in February 2026 in a round led by Aavishkaar Capital. It had previously raised Rs 60 crore in a Series A round in 2024.
On the lender side, Credgenics has raised $50 million and provides technology for collections, litigation management and online dispute resolution. CreditNirvana, a Perfios company, launched its agentic AI platform Maestro for debt collections in November 2025 and introduced an integrated AI suite for collections and lending in October 2026.
CredResolve, an AI-powered debt collections infrastructure startup, raised a pre-Series A round led by Merak Ventures in April 2026 to expand its operations, multilingual AI and voice capabilities.

title: Med-tech startup Sunfox Technologies raises $7 Mn in Series A round
summary:
Sunfox Technologies, the Dehradun-based medtech company behind the Spandan portable ECG platform, has raised $7 million (approx. Rs 67 crore) in a Series A funding round co-led by Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, Alchemy Capital and 3one4 Capital.
The startup had previously raised Rs 15 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Venture Catalysts, with participation from Finvolve through the IA Growth Opportunities Fund I and Brew Opportunities Fund, Universal Group, RP Singhvi Group and others in August 2024. It also secured investments from all five Sharks in the first season of Shark Tank India.
The fresh funds will be used for the next phase of growth, including expanding its presence across India, developing global go-to-market capabilities, scaling the organisation and continuing investments in research and development, Sunfox said in a press release.
Founded in 2016 by Rajat Jain, Arpit Jain, Saurabh Badola, Nitin Chandola and Sabit Rawat, Sunfox Technologies develops portable and AI-enabled healthcare solutions, with a focus on diagnostic access, particularly in cardiac care.
Its flagship Spandan series is a portable, medical-grade ECG platform designed for use across hospitals, clinics, telemedicine networks and home-based patient monitoring. The platform enables ECGs to be recorded closer to patients and can flag cardiac patterns that may require further medical attention.
Over the past decade, Sunfox has developed a range of Spandan ECG solutions for personal, clinical and institutional use, with applications across home-based ECG recording, clinics, hospitals, public-health programmes and remote-care networks.
Sunfox said it has expanded its presence to more than 15 countries, while its products have reached healthcare providers across more than 1,800 PIN codes in India. Its technology can also be deployed through a hub-and-spoke model in public-health systems.
The company said around 60,000 Spandan devices have been deployed across India, covering more than 20,000 villages across states and union territories. Its Spandan One platform has been used to screen approximately 5 million patients annually.
Sunfox competes with players such as AliveCor and Tricog in the cardiac monitoring and diagnostics space.
Meanwhile, Monitra Health has raised fresh capital this year for its remote cardiac monitoring platform. Beyond cardiac care, companies such as Molbio Diagnostics are expanding portable point-of-care diagnostics through its battery-operated Truenat platform.

title: Agentic AI startup Desible.ai raises Rs 32 Cr led by Prime Venture Partners
summary:
Bengaluru based AI startup Desible.ai has raised Rs 32 crore in a seed plus round led by Prime Venture Partners, with participation from existing investor Invention Engine. 
The proceeds will be used to expand its agentic AI capabilities, strengthen compliance infrastructure and accelerate product development for the BFSI sector.
Founded in 2025 by Uttam Tiwari and Omkar Raikar, Desible.ai provides an agentic workflow orchestration platform for banks, NBFCs and insurance companies. The platform helps automate customer engagement, servicing, operations and compliance workflows, starting with voice and expanding to WhatsApp, SMS and email.
Desible.ai currently works with more than 40 BFSI institutions and runs over 25 agentic workflows across revenue, risk and compliance, collections, underwriting, service and claims. The company said its platform handles more than 1 crore customer engagements every month and integrates with existing enterprise systems.
The startup is built around deterministic decision-making, with workflows designed to ensure that disclosures, consent and escalations follow predefined rules and remain auditable. 
Its use cases include collections, lead qualification, renewal management, claims intimation, welcome calling, TeleMER and cross-sell.

title: Edtech startup byteXL raises $9 Mn in funding round led by Elevar Equity
summary:
Edtech startup byteXL has raised $9 million in its latest funding round led by Elevar Equity, with participation from existing investors Kalaari Capital and the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation. 
The latest round follows byteXL’s $5.9 million Series A raised in July 2024 from Kalaari Capital and the Dell Foundation. 
The fresh capital will be used to expand its institutional network, strengthen its AI and technology platform, and develop new skilling programmes. byteXL also plans to invest in AI enabled learning and assessment, student analytics and personalised learning tools.
Founded by brothers Karun and Sricharan Tadepalli, byteXL works with engineering colleges, particularly in tier 2 and tier 3 cities, to provide technology and AI skills alongside regular academic education. 
Its model combines industry aligned curriculum, practical learning, technology platforms and trained educators within college programmes.
The company claims 7,600 byteXL graduates were placed in IT and engineering roles last year. It currently reaches around 2 lakh students through 40 institutions and plans to expand to 120 institutions and 5 lakh students across 15 states over the next two years.

title: JioHotstar expands to MENA through STARZPLAY
summary:
JioHotstar, the streaming platform owned by JioStar, has expanded its international presence to the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) through a partnership with streaming platform STARZPLAY.
As part of the partnership, JioHotstar will be available as a dedicated streaming destination on the STARZPLAY app and website across the MENA region.
The offering will include JioHotstar Originals alongside their India release, television content from JioStar channels, films and reality shows. The content will be available in multiple languages, including Hindi, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu and Bangla. It will also include the upcoming season of Koffee with Karan and the ongoing season of Bigg Boss across six languages.
JioHotstar will be available through STARZPLAY’s PLUS plan at AED 34.99 ($9.5) per month. The MAX plan, priced at AED 49.99 ($13.6) per month, will combine the JioHotstar catalogue with STARZPLAY’s sports offering.
The MENA launch comes about a month after JioHotstar expanded beyond India into the UK, Canada and Singapore. The platform launched in these three markets in September with more than 160,000 hours of entertainment across 12 plus Asian languages, covering films, television, originals, regional programming, reality shows, kids’ content and anime.
The platform had also introduced quarterly and annual subscription plans in the three markets, with existing Hotstar subscribers transitioning to equivalent JioHotstar plans.
JioHotstar said its MENA offering will have a substantial Malayalam catalogue, given the region’s Malayali audience. The company is also positioning the service around South Asian audiences in the region, while seeking to reach a wider audience interested in Indian entertainment.
Amit Malhotra, Head of International Business at JioStar, said the company sees MENA as a key market given its large South Asian diaspora and demand for multilingual entertainment.
Maaz Sheikh, CEO of STARZPLAY, said the partnership will combine JioHotstar’s Indian content catalogue with STARZPLAY’s regional reach and streaming capabilities.
JioHotstar currently claims more than 500 million monthly active users and a library of over 300,000 hours of programming across 19 languages.
The company has been expanding its international footprint as part of its strategy to build JioHotstar into a global streaming platform. The September launch marked its first major international rollout under the JioHotstar brand, with the service becoming available in the UK, Canada and Singapore.

title: TPG-backed NewQuest offloads Rs 115 Cr Shadowfax stake in bulk deal
summary:
TPG-backed NewQuest Asia Fund IV has sold another 40 lakh shares of logistics company Shadowfax Technologies in a bulk deal worth Rs 114.8 crore.
According to exchange data, NewQuest Asia Fund IV (Singapore) sold the shares at Rs 287 per share, representing around 0.68% of Shadowfax’s paid-up equity capital.
This marks the fourth time that the private equity investor has offloaded shares of Shadowfax in the past three months. In August, NewQuest sold 1.25 crore shares worth around Rs 300.6 crore. It followed this with another sale of 80 lakh shares for nearly Rs 200 crore in September. On September 30, the investor sold another 40 lakh shares for Rs 113.6 crore.
With the latest transaction, NewQuest has sold 2.85 crore Shadowfax shares since July, reducing its stake by around 4.86 percentage points. It held an 11.53% stake in the company as of June 2026.
The logistics company has also reported strong financial performance. Its consolidated net profit surged more than eightfold to Rs 65.4 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 8 crore in the year-ago period. Operating revenue rose 65% year-on-year to Rs 1,358 crore during the quarter.
Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Bansal and Vaibhav Khandelwal, Shadowfax provides logistics services to e-commerce, quick-commerce and D2C companies. The company was listed on the stock exchanges earlier this year at an IPO price of Rs 124 per share.
The company currently operates across more than 16,000 pincodes and is expanding its quick-commerce network as it looks to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing last-mile delivery market.
The shares of the firm are currently trading at Rs 287.6 as of (10.38 AM, with a total market capitalization of Rs 16,895 crore.

title: Zomint raises Rs 36 Cr seed round from Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners
summary:
Wealth management startup Zomint has raised Rs 36 crore ($3.75 million) in a seed round from Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners. 
The proceeds will be used to expand its wealth and investment teams, strengthen its technology platform and build its investor education ecosystem.
Founded in September 2025 by Aman Mittal and Shavir Bansal, Zomint offers wealth management services to working professionals and families. Investors can start with a monthly SIP of Rs 25,000 or a lump sum investment of Rs 5 lakh.
Zomint assigns each family a personal wealth expert who tracks their investments and financial goals. The expert is supported by investment research and AI tools that bring together portfolio information, past conversations and research, flag areas that need attention and track agreed actions.
The firm claims it has retained 97% of its clients since launch, despite market volatility. Nearly one in three clients made additional investments through the platform within three months of their initial engagement. Its relationship managers currently serve more than 250 families each, supported by investment specialists and AI enabled tools.
Zomint acquired its customers entirely through organic content, using the founders’ financial content platform Bekifaayati, which has more than 50 lakh subscribers.

title: Chiratae Ventures leads $10 Mn round in photonic quantum startup Quanfluence
summary:
Photonic quantum technology startup Quanfluence has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Chiratae Ventures, with participation from Rainmatter by Zerodha and existing investor Pi Ventures.
The Bengaluru-based startup had earlier raised $2 million in a seed round led by Pi Ventures, with participation from Golden Sparrow, Reena Dayal and others in December 2024.
The fresh funds will be used to build and launch a four-qubit quantum computer in the near term, with the company targeting a larger prototype featuring around 100 qubits by 2029, Quanfluence said in a press release.
Founded in 2021 by Sujoy Chakravarty, Ravi Mehta, Biman Chattopadhyay, Anil Prabhakar, Aditi Vaidya and Sandeep Goyal, Quanfluence develops photonic quantum computing technology for optimisation problems. Its hardware-based solution is designed to complement AI in decision-making.
The company aims to develop a fault-tolerant, general-purpose quantum computer over the next five to six years.
Unlike conventional quantum computing systems that require complex cooling infrastructure, Quanfluence’s technology combines optics and hardware to operate at room temperature. Its optical Ising machine uses light waves and FPGAs for optimisation processing, which the company claims can be up to 100 times faster than classical computing for certain workloads.
The startup’s system is designed to address high-dimensional optimisation problems across areas such as logistics, workforce scheduling, risk management and financial optimisation.
Quanfluence is also testing an advanced version of its system capable of processing 10-25 million permutations for complex optimisation problems, including financial risk management, logistics and delivery route planning.
The sector has been gaining traction amid the government’s Rs 6,003.65-crore National Quantum Mission, which includes photonic technologies among the platforms being developed for quantum computing.
Other startups in the space have also attracted investor interest. QpiAI raised $32 million in Series A funding last year from Avataar Ventures and the National Quantum Mission, while BQP, formerly known as BosonQ Psi, raised about $5 million in seed funding this year for its quantum-inspired simulation technology.
QuBeats, another deeptech startup working on quantum sensing and advanced laser technologies, raised $15 million in its first institutional round in April from Zoho Corporation, Indusbridge Ventures and the National Quantum Mission, along with government grant support.
